patches.why: the plate prints 'concilio' — c-o-n-c-i-l-i-o, unambiguous at full resolution on leaf n310. Corpus Corporum altered it to 'consilio', which is a different word: concilium is an assembly or council, consilium a purpose or counsel. Restoring Migne's reading; the translator judged the printed word SOUND rather than defective (concilium/consilium is an attested medieval orthographic interchange, Pattern 9), so no [sic:] is stacked on it — the English renders concilium's own sense.
